summary: This workflow reads a members CSV file, keeps only rows where status is Active, renames and drops a couple of columns, then writes the result to an output CSV. It scores 2 out of 10, meaning it is a direct translation to SQL with no design decisions needed. All four tools are simple, low-difficulty operations that map one-to-one onto standard SQL clauses.

key_components.description: Loads member data from a CSV file, which becomes a COPY from S3 or an existing table in Redshift.
Filters rows to only those with status equal to Active, which becomes a WHERE clause.
Renames the plan_type column to plan and drops two other columns, which becomes a column list with aliases in the SELECT.
Writes the final result to a CSV output, which becomes a CREATE TABLE AS, INSERT INTO, or UNLOAD to S3.

risks.title: CSV source has no defined data types
risks.detail: The input file is a CSV, which carries no column data types. When loading with COPY into Redshift, column types must be explicitly defined to avoid type mismatches or load errors.
